```{r}
#| include: false
## library to inspect objects
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(rlang)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(ggtext)
library(gghighlight)
library(patchwork)
```

[Q. Difference between `geom_path()` and `geom_line()`]{.question} `geom_path` connects in the order the points appear.
Both recognize `linetype`

[Q. Difference between `geom_rect()` and `geom_tile()`?]{.question} `geom_rect()` has `xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax` whereas `geom_tile()` 
measures coordinates from the center of the rectangle. It has `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`. `geom_raster()` is a [fast special case]{.warning} of `geom_tile()`

(@) `geom_area()` is a good way to color area below the plot.


```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  x = c(3 ,1, 5),
  y = c(2,-4,6),
  label = c("a", "b", "c")
)

df |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, label = label)) +
  geom_area(color = "gray", alpha = 0.7)

```

[Q. How to group based on more than one column?]{.question} Use `aes(group = interaction(school_id, student_id))` 

[Q. How to interpolate more values of y based on interpolated values of x?]{.question}

```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 11:13, color = c(1,3,5))

xgrid <- with(df , seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 10))
xgrid

approx(df$x, df$y, xout = xgrid)
```

(@) [Default `group` asthetics]{.key} `fill` or `color` aesthetic using a [discrete]{.warning} variable makes the variable a `group`
aesthetic as well. So applying `aes(fill = discrete_val)` makes groups the data based on `discrete_val`. This is NOT true when
using a continuous variable for the `fill` asthetic. 


```{r}
# drv is character therefore treated equivalently to factor.
# Here, drv is also a group asthetic. So, for the finest grain grouping the values of fill aesthetic is the same. 
# Hence, they have the same color.
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(class, fill = drv)) +
  geom_bar()

# Here, the latest grouping is `class`. For each group in class, there are multiple fill colors, so ggplot ignores individual
# color mappings altogether and gives a default gray color to all.
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(class, fill = hwy )) + 
  geom_bar()

# Need to explicitly mention group aesthetic for continuous fill aesthetics.
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(class, fill = hwy, group = hwy)) +
  geom_bar()

```

(@) Different methods to display **uncertainty**.


```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c(18, 11, 16), se = c(1.2, 0.5, 1.0))
cb <- df |> ggplot(aes(x, y, ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se)) + geom_crossbar()
lr <- df |> ggplot(aes(x, y, ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se)) + geom_linerange() + geom_point()
sm <- df |> ggplot(aes(x, y, ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se)) + geom_smooth(stat = "identity")
rb <- df |> ggplot(aes(x, y, ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se)) + geom_ribbon()

cb + lr + sm + rb

```

(@) `bind_2d()` to show distribution . Use `fill = after_stat(density)` 
to use density instead of count.

```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(2000), y =  rnorm(2000))

df |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_bin2d(aes(fill = after_stat(density)))
```

[Q. How to use some other summary function instead of the default count in `geom_bar`?]{.question}

```{r}
diamonds |>
  ggplot(aes(color, price)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "summary_bin", fun = mean)
```

(@) Use `quote()` to include formulas in axis titles


```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = seq(-2, 2, by = 0.01))
df |>
  ggplot(aes(x)) +
  stat_function(aes(colour = "first"), geom = "point", fun = \(x) x^3) +
  ylab(label = quote(f(x) == x^3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("first" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal()

```

(@) Use the `ggtext::element_markdown()` type for the text themes to include bold or italic type.


```{r}
data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 1:3, family = c("sans", "serif", "mono"), fontface = c("plain", "bold", "italic")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x,y)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = family, family = family, fontface = fontface)) +
  xlab(label = "Axis title with *italic* and **bold**") +
  theme(axis.title.x = ggtext::element_markdown())
```

(@) Coloring the background with `geom_rect(aes(fill=))`


```{r}
presidential <- subset(presidential, start > economics$date[1])

economics |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_vline(data = presidential, aes(xintercept = start), colour = "grey50", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_rect(data = presidential, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, fill = party), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = presidential, aes(x = start, label = name), y = 2500, nudge_x = 50, hjust = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(date, unemploy)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Republican" = "red", "Democratic" = "blue")) +
  theme_minimal()

```
(@) Use `annotate(geom = "text")` or with `geom = "point"` to add individual annotations.

```{r}
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point(
    data = filter(mpg, manufacturer == "subaru"),
    colour = "orange",
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  annotate( geom = "point", x = 5.5, y = 40, colour = "orange", size = 3) +
  annotate( geom = "point", x = 5.5, y = 40) +
  annotate( geom = "text", x = 5.6, y = 40, label = "Subaru", hjust = "left")
```

(@) Using `gghighlight::gghighlight()` to highlight important parts of the plot


```{r}
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(displ, hwy, colour = factor(cyl)))  +
  geom_point() +
  gghighlight::gghighlight() +
  facet_wrap(vars(cyl))
```

# Using `patchwork`

(@) **Key rules**
  - Use `plot_layout(ncol = 2)`  to explicitly set the alignment
  - `/` for rows and `|` for columns
  - use `plot_layout(design = strlayout)` for complicated layouts 
  - Can collect guides using `guides = "collect"`

```{r}
p1 <- mpg |> ggplot() + geom_point(aes(displ, hwy))
p2 <- mpg |> ggplot() + geom_bar(aes(year, fill = drv), position = "dodge")
p3 <- mpg |> ggplot() + geom_density(aes(hwy, fill = drv), color = NA) + facet_grid(rows = vars(drv))
p4 <- mpg |> ggplot() + 
  stat_summary(aes(x = drv, y = hwy, fill = drv), fun.data = mean_se, geom = "col")

p3 + p1 + p2 + plot_layout(ncol = 2)
p3 | (p2 / (p1 | p4))

# collecting guides and placing them into the 4th slot
p1 + p2 + p3 + guide_area() + plot_layout(ncol = 2, guides = "collect") 

```

# Scales

(@) [Position scales]{.key} managed by `scale_x_continuous` .

  - set limits using `scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA))`. Use `NA` for default limit on one side. 
  - If limits for both axes need to be set, a [shortcut]{.warning} is `lims(x = c(10,20), y = (0, NA))`. 
  - Can use `xlim()` and `ylim()` for a single position scale.

[Q. Difference between `coord_cartesian(ylim = c(10, 35))` and `lims(y = c(10, 35))`?]{.question} `coord_cartesian` **zooms** whereas `lims` sets the values
outside the set limits to `NA`.


```{r}
base <- mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(drv, hwy)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 28, colour = "red") +
  geom_boxplot()+
  theme_minimal()

# lims here incorrectly pushes the median down by setting some of the outliers to 0.
base | (base + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(10,35))) | (base + lims(y = c(10,35)))
```

(@) Axis and legend [tick marks]{.warning} are [scale breaks]{.key}. 

  -  Set using `scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL)` or `breaks = scales::breaks_width(800, offset = 200)`.
  - The above example creates ticks with equal spaces of 800 but starting with 1000.

```{r}
toy <- data.frame(
  const = 1, up = 1:4, txt = letters[1:4],  big = (1:4)* 1000, log = c(2, 5, 10, 2000)
)

toy |>
  ggplot(aes(big, const)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  # No ticks on the y axis
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  # minor grid lines are added automatically
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(800, offset = 200))
```
(@) Handy way to create matrix with combinations
```{r}
1:10 %o% 10 ^ (0:3)
```

(@) Create [minor breaks]{.key} with `minor_break` argument. This is handy when the log scale is involved.

```{r}
mb <- 1:10 %o% 10 ^ (0:3) |> as.numeric() |> unique()
toy |>
  ggplot(aes(log, const)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  # scale_x_log10(minor_breaks = mb)
# The below is equivalent to scale_x_log10 for which the trans = "log" value is preset
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10", minor_breaks = mb)
```
(@) Every shortcut position scale such as `scale_x_log10` has a corresponding `trans` values to be set in `scale_x_continuous`


```{r}
diamonds |>
  ggplot(aes(price, carat)) +
  geom_bin2d() +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10") +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10")
```

(@) Use the special `date_breaks` and `date_labels` for `scale_x_date`. 
  - Use the original `breaks` and `labels` parameters if further customization is required.

```{r}
date_base <- economics |>
  ggplot(aes(date, psavert)) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)

(date_base + scale_x_date(date_breaks = "5 years", date_labels = "%y")) |
# This is the same as using date_breaks and date_labels
(date_base + scale_x_date(breaks = scales::breaks_width("5 years"), labels = scales::label_date("%y")))
```

(@) Use `guides()` to align labels


```{r}
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(manufacturer, hwy)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  guides(x = guide_axis(angle = 45))
```
(@) Specify a colour scale using `scale_fill_viridis_c()`

```{r}
dist <- faithfuld |>
  ggplot(aes(eruptions, waiting)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = density)) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = NULL, expand = 0) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = NULL, expand = 0) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

dist | dist + scale_fill_viridis_c() | dist + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma")
```

(@) use `na.value = "yellow"` to set what happens for `NA` values in the column used to fill color


```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = 1, y = 1:5, z = c(1,2,3,NA, 5))
first <- df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x, y, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = 0, labels = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = 0) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

(first | first + scale_fill_continuous(na.value = "yellow") | first + scale_fill_continuous(na.value = NA)) & theme_minimal()
```
